archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A small, quick-twitch passer whose value in Minnesota comes from accurate short throws and from turning broken plays into first downs with his legs, at the cost of a lot of sacks.

report.headline: Climbing out of a bad start, but the sacks and the hamstring cap him
report.take:
Murray in Minnesota is a low-volume dual-threat quarterback on a team built around the league's best defense. The Vikings pass less than the situation calls for (-2.8 pass rate over expected), their offense ranks 29th in EPA, and he is averaging 25.7 attempts a game. His season passing line, -0.059 EPA per dropback (31st of 47), looks like a below-average starter. That number mixes two different quarterbacks. One is the passer of Week 1, when he played 17% of snaps, and of Week 3 at Tampa Bay, which now ranks second on defense; he lost 12.1 EPA that day. The other is the passer of the last three games, at +0.079 per dropback and 7.45 adjusted net yards per dropback, both comfortably above the league average.

The arm is not what holds him back. Throws 0-9 yards out are completing at 80.3% with a +9.8 CPOE, and his throws of 10+ air yards carry +0.167 EPA. His bad-throw rate is down to 10.4% from 15.5% last year. The drain sits in two places. Throws behind the line, the screens and swing passes, have cost -16.8 EPA on 33 attempts. Those are largely a scheme and blocking problem. The second is sacks: 8.9% of dropbacks, 38th of 47, even though he is pressured on only 19.3% of them, 12th-lowest. When pressure does come, 37.5% of it ends in a sack.

That sack habit belongs to him. His pressure-to-sack rate has sat at or above 0.30 in most seasons and hit 0.50 last year. This year his time to throw is 2.95 seconds, the longest of his career, up 0.27 on last season. He is holding the ball to hunt for something or to escape, and the escapes pay. His 16 scrambles average +0.757 EPA and have produced 8 first downs, and his 27.8 rushing yards a game rank fifth among quarterbacks. The trade is close to a wash: the legs and the extended plays roughly pay for the sacks, and that is why the per-dropback number hovers near average once the two outlier games fall away.

The split that best describes the offense is shotgun at -0.214 EPA against under center at +0.189. Kevin O'Connell's play-action and under-center menu suits Murray, while obvious passing downs expose him: third downs sit at -0.302 EPA with an average of 8.1 yards to go. The direction from here is a passer settling in, at average or slightly better, on modest volume. Fantasy production leans on his legs and on T.J. Hockenson, whose +0.611 EPA per target is carrying the passing game. All of that hinges on a hamstring injury that a scrambler cannot ignore.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for themselves
strengths.body: He has scrambled on 8.6% of dropbacks, and those plays have been among the most efficient in the offense, with half of them moving the chains. This is his career signature: he ranked top-four in rushing yards among quarterbacks in four of his Arizona seasons. It lasts as long as the hamstring lets it.

strengths.title: Precise in the short game
strengths.body: Between the line and 9 air yards he is completing 80.3% of his throws, nearly 10 points over expectation, and his bad-throw rate has dropped to seventh-best. His overall CPOE of +2.06 matches his better Arizona years (2020, 2021, 2024) rather than last year's dip. It looks real.

strengths.title: Three-game climb is substantive
strengths.body: Over his last three games he is at +0.079 EPA per dropback, 0.138 better than his season. His TD rate has risen to 4.8% and his INT rate fallen to 1.2%. The schedule helped (New Orleans, Indianapolis and Detroit all rank 23rd or worse on defense now). The improvement also came with his aggressiveness rising to 27.6% at Detroit, so he is starting to push the ball.

concerns.title: Holding the ball into sacks
concerns.body: He takes an 8.9% sack rate behind a line that rarely lets pressure in, so the sacks are mostly his. His career-long 2.95-second time to throw has made it worse. It is a trait he has carried for years, so expect it to persist. It is a partial cost of the scramble value, not a pure flaw, but it turns third-and-medium into punts.

concerns.title: Third downs and shotgun drain
concerns.body: The offense falls apart when it is predictable. Third downs have cost -17.5 EPA and shotgun snaps -27.8, while under-center snaps are positive. It reflects a run game ranked 28th that leaves long yardage, plus his tendency to hold the ball. It is unlikely to fix itself quickly.

concerns.title: Screen game bleeding points
concerns.body: Throws behind the line have produced -0.508 EPA per play, which wipes out the gains he makes on short throws. That is mostly scheme and blocking, along with Aaron Jones' -0.145 EPA per target, rather than his accuracy. It is the most fixable leak on the list.

trend.note: A brief Week 1 and a rough day at Tampa Bay sank the season line. Since then he has posted positive or near-neutral passing EPA every week, peaking at +8.9 in New Orleans.

nextGame.headline: Soft Bills pass defense, if the hamstring cooperates
nextGame.body:
Buffalo's defense ranks 28th in EPA and 26th against the pass. It allows the fifth-most explosive pass rate and has given opposing WR1s more over their averages than any defense in the league. That sets up Justin Jefferson, whose +0.323 EPA per target is the second-best of Murray's options. The Bills hit quarterbacks often (fourth in hit rate) but rarely finish, ranking 25th in sack rate. That plays to a quarterback who escapes. It is also a script risk: Buffalo's offense ranks first in EPA, the Vikings are 3.5-point home underdogs, and a game where they chase points could push his volume up and his sack count with it. The game is indoors.

Availability is the story. Murray is questionable with a hamstring and undergoing a full evaluation as of November 2. Even if he plays, a sore hamstring threatens the scrambling that makes his profile work. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw (92% of snaps) is also questionable with a shoulder, and losing him would hurt a quarterback already prone to sacks. On Buffalo's side, nickel corner Dee Alford (54% of snaps) sat out last week with an ankle injury, which thins the coverage on the slot and middle of the field where Murray throws well.

keyMatchups.title: Jefferson against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo ranks last in WR1 points over average and 27th in EPA per play allowed to them. Murray's targeting has leaned on Hockenson, but this matchup invites him to feed Jefferson outside.

keyMatchups.title: Hockenson over the middle
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo allows 0.4 EPA per play to tight ends (26th), and Alford's absence weakens the coverage underneath. Hockenson has been Murray's most productive target by a wide margin.

keyMatchups.title: Hits without sacks
keyMatchups.body: The Bills reach the quarterback but rarely bring him down. That suits Murray's habit of extending plays, provided Darrisaw plays and the hamstring allows him to escape.

nextGame.watch: Whether he scrambles freely early. A hesitant, pocket-bound Murray loses the part of his game that offsets the sacks.

restOfSeason.body:
The realistic baseline is the post-Week 3 version: roughly league-average efficiency on low volume, because the Vikings win with defense and keep the ball on the ground. Expect around 170-215 passing yards a game. His touchdown rate should drift up from 3.2% toward his last-three level as the red-zone completion rate holds. His rushing, 25-40 yards a game, is the most dependable part of his fantasy value, as long as the hamstring heals. The sack rate will stay high because it has followed him for his whole career. The -16.8 EPA on throws behind the line should shrink with better design, which is the main source of upside.

The hard limits are volume and health. His team has the top-ranked defense, so blowouts and comebacks are rare and the game script rarely forces him to throw 35 times. He has also missed significant time in four of the last five seasons, so a lingering hamstring problem is a real risk rather than a footnote.
swingFactors: Hamstring recovery and its effect on scrambling
Darrisaw's availability on the left side
Whether the screen game and third downs get fixed

confidence.note: Six games with one partial, a clear upward trend, but the hamstring could change everything.
